title: How Much Does Branding Cost? (What $3k Actually Buys)
description: Founder-facing branding cost map: what a $3,000 senior Brand Sprint buys vs sub-$3k marketplace clutter (~$750 direction kits / $1.5k–$2.3k sprints), $15k peers, Primary $50k, and $25k–$100k+ agencies — scopes, not survey averages.
body:
Search "how much does branding cost" and you get answers from a few hundred dollars to six figures.

Most of those pages bury the only question that matters: what scope are you actually buying?

This guide is for founders, owners, and marketers who need cost clarity before they hire — not a designer tutorial.

I'm Arek Dvornechuck, a senior brand designer in New York.

I run Ebaq Design as a one-person senior studio: you work with me directly.

Key takeaways

  • "Branding cost" is usually one of four jobs: logo only, core identity, identity plus website, or a multi-month rebrand.
  • Compare scopes, not sticker totals.
  • Logo-only pricing lives in How Much Does a Logo Cost?.
  • Ebaq's Brand Sprint is $3,000 / about one week, senior-direct.
  • Sub-$3k marketplace clutter now runs from direction sprints as low as about $750, through 72-hour identity sprints around $900, to one- and two-week brand sprints roughly $1,500–$2,300 on public Contra listings (October 2026) — that is market noise, not the same product. Compare seniority, motion, and interactive web, not just the sticker.
  • Mid-tier sprint peers publicly state about $15k / 2 weeks (Proof of Work, PIXELUP); Primary states a flat $50k / 2 weeks.
  • NYC agency Splash Creative now lists Focused identity around $8k, Identity around $12k, Brand + Web $25k–$75k, and a $7,500 two-week AI Implementation Sprint.
  • Traditional agencies on Ebaq's Comparison sit at $25k–$100k+ and 3–9 months; NYC agency Crafted has published $25k–$60k focused and $100k+ full brand-and-build.
  • Ongoing work with me starts at $10k/mo when you need a retained partner.

Start with scope, not a dollar number

Before you compare prices, name the job.

JobWhat you are buyingRough shape
Logo onlyA mark and file packageSee logo design cost
Core identityLogo system, type, color, usable guidelinesSprint / package territory
Identity + websiteBrand system plus a marketed siteTwo scopes (or a combined package)
Full rebrand programStrategy, identity, rollout, often web + collateral over monthsAgency / long engagement

If two quotes differ by 5×, they are almost never the same product.

For package contents in practice, also see branding package.

Brand + website add-ons (competitor-stated, when peers publish them):

  • Proof of Work: brand + web together $25k–$35k on their startup rebrand cost page; a separate what is a brand sprint page also cites $40k combined — attribute to the page you are reading.
  • PIXELUP: brand + website $25k–$40k on their cost blog.

Those figures are their public claims for their scopes — not Ebaq quotes and not survey math.

Ebaq's live numbers remain: $3k Brand Sprint / ~1 week, from $10k/mo ongoing, vs agency $25k–$100k+ on the homepage Comparison.

What $3,000 actually buys

The Brand Sprint is for founders past DIY and marketplace roulette who need a core identity, not a six-month agency program.

In about one week, the core engagement typically covers:

  • Custom logo system (primary mark and practical lockups)
  • Color palette and typography direction
  • An online style guide your team can use
  • Key brand assets agreed for the sprint
  • Direct work with me — senior designer, no junior handoff
  • Revisions inside the sprint scope

Homepage framing, same idea: custom logo, type & colors, style guide & key brand assets, work directly with Arek.

It is not research theater with three account layers.

It is a focused identity you can put on a site, deck, and product UI without guessing hex codes in Slack.

Why not a $1,500 sprint?

The low end of the market got louder in 2026.

Public Contra listings now include direction sprints as low as about $750, 72-hour identity sprints around $900, and one- to two-week brand sprints roughly $1,500–$2,300.

Some branding sites go even lower. Brandframer, for example, publishes packages around $280–$987 (their pricing, not Ebaq's).

Those are other sellers' offers — market noise to calibrate against, not what Ebaq sells.

The label is the same. The job often is not.

What the $3,000 Brand Sprint adds:

  • Senior-direct work — you work with me, a senior designer in New York, from strategy to final files.
  • Built to move — I design identities with motion in mind, and I do brand motion myself, so the system holds up in logo animation, product UI, and launch video.
  • Built for interactive web — I design and build Framer, Webflow, and React sites, so the identity is made to live on a real site, not just a PDF.
  • No vendor restart — when you add motion or a website later, the same person carries the system forward.

If all you need is a mark and a palette this week, a cheaper listing may be fine.

If the brand has to win buyers, investors, and hires — and look different from every peer — compare what ships, not the sticker.

What $3k does not buy

Usually out of the core Brand Sprint unless we scope them separately:

  • Full marketing website design/build (Framer, Webflow, or React)
  • Large illustration or photography production
  • Packaging, vehicles, environmental graphics
  • Heavy motion beyond what we agree for the sprint
  • Unlimited multi-quarter retainers (that is the $10k/mo path)

If you need brand and site together, use a buyer checklist like branding and website redesign scope and book a call so both are sized honestly.

Peers who publish brand+web bands (Proof of Work $25–35k, PIXELUP $25–40k) are selling a wider job than a one-week identity sprint — again, compare scopes.

When $10k/mo makes more sense

A sprint is a clear identity outcome with a hard edge.

Ongoing from $10,000/month fits when you need a senior design partner week after week: product marketing surfaces, launch systems, iteration after the first identity lands.

Same person. Different container.

How to compare any branding quote

Force every proposal onto one page:

  1. Deliverables — logo only, identity system, messaging, website, guidelines depth?
  2. Who does the work — named senior, or juniors behind an account manager?
  3. Timeline — calendar weeks to usable files.
  4. Revisions and ownership — limits, source files, usage rights.
  5. What is explicitly out — so "$X branding" does not secretly mean logo-only.

FAQ

How much does branding cost for a small business?

Enough to buy a usable identity system, not just a JPEG.

Ebaq's core Brand Sprint is $3,000 for about one week.

Agency programs on our Comparison commonly sit at $25k–$100k+.

Logo-only budgets belong in the logo design cost guide.

Is $3,000 enough for a real brand identity?

For core identity — logo system, type, color, guide, key assets — yes, when scope stays honest and the designer is senior and direct.

It is not enough if you also expect a full custom website, packaging line, and campaign system in the same week.

Why are some one-week brand sprints under $3,000?

Marketplace clutter under $3k now spans lighter direction kits from about $750, 72-hour sprints around $900, and one- to two-week brand sprints roughly $1,500–$2,300 — sellers compete on price.

Outside marketplaces, some sites publish packages as low as about $280–$987 (Brandframer). That is another seller's pricing, not an Ebaq option.

Before you compare them to a $3,000 senior sprint, ask who actually designs, how deep the system goes, and whether motion or a website can follow without a new vendor.

Ebaq does not price under the $3,000 Brand Sprint — the difference is senior judgment plus motion and interactive web in one studio.

Why do some brand sprints cost $15k or $50k?

Different studios package different teams, research depth, and inclusions.

  • Proof of Work states $15,000 flat / 2 weeks for their Brand Sprint.
  • Splash Creative lists Focused ~$8k, Identity ~$12k, and a $7,500 two-week AI Implementation Sprint.
  • PIXELUP states a Brand Sprint starting at $15,000 (~2 weeks on their cost blog).
  • Primary states a flat $50k / 2 weeks.
  • At the agency end, Crafted has published $25k–$60k focused and $100k+ full brand-and-build.

Those are competitor-stated offers for their scopes — useful for mapping the market, not a claim every business needs that band.

What about Metabrand's $4,490 packages?

Metabrand publishes exact SKUs on their startup offer: Brand Identity $4,490, Website $4,490, Complete $8,390.

They also publish separate FAQ engagement ranges (about $15k–$65k on their tech branding page).

Do not collapse those into one "average." Compare the SKU line items to what you need.

Does Slam publish a fixed brand-sprint price?

No fixed public sprint sticker on their rebrand service page.

Their content cites typical startup brand engagements around $15k–$50k (startup brand agency), with focused rebrands often 8–16 weeks (rebranding agency) — useful range language, not a SKU.

Should I hire an agency or a senior freelancer?

Hire the smallest team that can own the work end-to-end.

If you want speed, taste, and one throat to choke, a senior sprint beats a multi-month agency for most early-stage brands.

If you need enterprise process across many workstreams, agency math can make sense — budget for $25k–$100k+ and months.

Can I start with branding and add a website later?

Yes.

The $3,000 core identity can stand alone; website is additional scope.

Many clients ship identity first, then build Framer/Webflow/React next.

How do I know if I need a rebrand vs a refresh before I spend?

Use Should You Rebrand? before you commission anything.

A new identity will not fix an unclear offer.
